questions.stem: This surgical illustration depicts an open operation at the carotid bifurcation in which the artery is incised and the diseased intimal plaque is dissected free and removed, restoring the lumen. What is this procedure called?

explanation.summary: Endarterectomy removes the atheromatous plaque and inner arterial layer through an open arteriotomy, directly relieving high-grade stenosis in symptomatic patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endarterectomy removes the atheromatous plaque and inner arterial layer through an open arteriotomy, directly relieving high-grade stenosis in symptomatic patients.

questions.stem: On this non-contrast head CT, the red arrow points to an ill-defined area of decreased attenuation in the right hemisphere. What does this finding most likely represent?

choices.label: B
choices.text: An acute ischemic infarct in the middle cerebral artery territory

explanation.summary: Loss of gray-white differentiation and hypodensity mark an evolving ischemic infarct; here an embolus of carotid origin has occluded the right middle cerebral artery. Hemorrhage would appear hyperdense (bright).
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of gray-white differentiation and hypodensity mark an evolving ischemic infarct; here an embolus of carotid origin has occluded the right middle cerebral artery. Hemorrhage would appear hyperdense (bright).

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows a longitudinally opened common carotid artery at its bifurcation, with a bulky, irregular yellow-tan mass narrowing the lumen. What is the primary pathological process responsible for the narrowing?

explanation.summary: The specimen demonstrates a large atherosclerotic plaque at the carotid bifurcation, the classic site of carotid stenosis. Lipid-laden plaque encroaches on the lumen and can ulcerate to shed emboli.
explanation.whyCorrect: The specimen demonstrates a large atherosclerotic plaque at the carotid bifurcation, the classic site of carotid stenosis. Lipid-laden plaque encroaches on the lumen and can ulcerate to shed emboli.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a fragment breaking off a lesion at the carotid bifurcation (inset) and traveling into the cerebral circulation of the head. What is the mechanism of the stroke being depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Artery-to-artery thromboembolism from the carotid to a cerebral artery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rupture of a berry aneurysm causing hemorrhage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small-vessel lipohyalinosis producing a lacunar infarct

explanation.summary: The image depicts an embolus arising from a ruptured carotid plaque that travels downstream to occlude an intracranial branch, the dominant mechanism of stroke in carotid disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The image depicts an embolus arising from a ruptured carotid plaque that travels downstream to occlude an intracranial branch, the dominant mechanism of stroke in carotid disease.
